title: Noetherian collapse of a supplied local ring tower diagram
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed preorder. Supply diagrams of commutative local rings $A_i\xrightarrow{f_i}B_i\xrightarrow{g_i}C_i$, local transition maps $a_{ji},b_{ji},c_{ji}$ for $i\le j$, and local cocones $\alpha_i:A_i\to A$, $\beta_i:B_i\to B$, $\gamma_i:C_i\to C$ to a tower of commutative local rings $A\xrightarrow f B\xrightarrow g C$. All squares commute, transitions respect identities and composition, and these cocones are ring colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A homomorphism of local rings is local when the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. Suppose $A_i$ is essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, $B_i$ over $A_i$, and $C_i$ over $B_i$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Suppose the canonical maps
$B_i\otimes_{A_i}A_j\to B_j$, $b\otimes a\mapsto b_{ji}(b)f_j(a)$, and $C_i\otimes_{B_i}B_j\to C_j$, $c\otimes b\mapsto c_{ji}(c)g_j(b)$, are localizations for every $i\le j$; suppose also that $B_i\otimes_{A_i}A\to B$, $b\otimes a\mapsto\beta_i(b)f(a)$, and $C_i\otimes_{B_i}B\to C$, $c\otimes b\mapsto\gamma_i(c)g(b)$, are localizations for every $i$. Tensor products have their usual induced ring structures [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Here a localization at a multiplicative subset $W$ sends $W$ to units, every target element is a fraction with numerator in the source and denominator in $W$, and a source element mapping to zero is killed by an element of $W$.
Then all the supplied rings $A_i,B_i,C_i$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and each composite $A_i\to C_i$ is essentially of finite type. Each $C_i$ is a localization of a finitely presented $A_i$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. On the same supplied diagrams the canonical maps $C_i\otimes_{A_i}A_j\to C_j$, $c\otimes a\mapsto c_{ji}(c)(g_jf_j)(a)$, and $C_i\otimes_{A_i}A\to C$, $c\otimes a\mapsto\gamma_i(c)(gf)(a)$, are localizations for all $i\le j$ and all $i$, respectively. The original cocones on $A_i$ and $C_i$ are algebraic colimits: every limit element comes from a stage, and two stage elements have the same limit image if and only if their images coincide at a common later stage. No replacement of the supplied diagrams or cocone maps is required.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), input ring Z; elementary integer ideal calculation

proof.text: Fix i. Apply Algebra.EssFiniteType.isNoetherianRing first over Z to A_i, then with the algebra structure of f_i to B_i over A_i, and then with the algebra structure of g_i to C_i over B_i. This Mathlib theorem is precisely the composite of finite-type Noetherian permanence and localization Noetherian permanence. The supplied rings and maps are unchanged.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), both sentences; Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre), approximation paragraphs

proof.text: For each i, RingHom.EssFiniteType.comp applied to f_i and g_i makes g_i f_i essentially of finite type. Use Algebra.essFiniteType_iff_exists_subalgebra to obtain a finite type A_i-subalgebra P of C_i and a submonoid W such that C_i is its localization. Since A_i is Noetherian by the preceding step, Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType makes P finitely presented. Take p to be the algebra map into P and q to be the subalgebra inclusion into C_i. Their composite is g_i f_i by construction. The localization structure gives W.IsLocalizationMap q.

Fix $i\le j$. Apply the six-ring tensor-localization tower transition statement to the towers $(A_i,B_i,C_i)$ and $(A_j,B_j,C_j)$, with $r=a_{ji}$, $s=b_{ji}$ and $t=c_{ji}$. Its first localization hypothesis is precisely the supplied $B_i\otimes_{A_i}A_j\to B_j$, and its second is the supplied $C_i\otimes_{B_i}B_j\to C_j$. The composite algebra structures are $g_if_i$ and $g_jf_j$; the commuting squares in the item give their compatibility. The cited conclusion is a localization $h:C_i\otimes_{A_i}A_j\to C_j$ satisfying $h(c\otimes a)=c_{ji}(c)(g_jf_j)(a)$. This is the required canonical ring map: pure tensors generate the tensor product additively, so two ring maps with this formula agree. Hence the required map on the supplied transition diagram is a localization. In Lean, the proved private wrapper RingHom.isTensorLocalizationSquare_comp installs the algebra structures of both composites and their scalar-tower instances, converts IsLocalizationMap to IsLocalization for each supplied comparison, applies Module.tensorLocalization_tower_transition, and converts its conclusion back to IsLocalizationMap.

source.place: Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre), proof: sentence composing the adjacent tensor localizations

proof.text: Fix $i$ again and apply the same six-ring statement to the towers $(A_i,B_i,C_i)$ and $(A,B,C)$, this time with $r=\alpha_i$, $s=\beta_i$ and $t=\gamma_i$. Both localization hypotheses are now exactly the two limit-comparison localizations assumed in the item; the cocone squares give compatibility. Its conclusion is a localization $h:C_i\otimes_{A_i}A\to C$ with $h(c\otimes a)=\gamma_i(c)(gf)(a)$. Additive generation by pure tensors again identifies $h$ with the specified canonical map. This application uses no Noetherianity or finite type hypothesis on $A,B,C$, and leaves all cocone maps unchanged.

source.place: Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre), tensor-localization composition argument, applied to a stage and the limit tower

proof.text: Regard the supplied small preorder $I$ as a category. It is filtered: nonemptiness supplies an object, directedness supplies common targets for any two objects, and parallel arrows in a preorder are already equal. Apply the elementwise filtered-colimit statement for commutative rings first to the supplied cocone $(A,(\alpha_i))$ and then to $(C,(\gamma_i))$. These are ring colimits by hypothesis. Clause (1) says that every element of $A$, respectively $C$, comes from a stage. Clause (2) says that equality of any two stage images is equivalent to equality at a common later stage; arrows in this category are exactly inequalities. These conclusions concern the actual supplied cocones. Together with steps 2 through 5 this proves every clause without replacing any diagram.
